segments.arabic: [670] حدثنا أحمد بن يونس قال: حدثنا زهير قال: حدثنا إسماعيل قال: سمعت قيسا قال: أخبرني أبو مسعود
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us. He said: Isma‘il related to us. He said: I heard Qays say: Abu Mas‘ud informed me:

segments.arabic: أن رجلا قال والله يا رسول الله إني لأتأخر عن صلاة الغداة من أجل فلان مما يطيل بنا فما رأيت رسول الله ﷺ في موعظة أشد غضبا منه يومئذ، ثم قال إن منكم منفرين فأيكم ما صلى بالناس فليتجوز فإن فيهم الضعيف والكبير وذا الحاجة
segments.english: That a man said: “By Allah, Messenger of Allah, I stay away from the morning prayer because of so-and-so, because he makes it so long for us.” I had never seen the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, more angry when giving admonition than he was that day. Then he said: “Some of you drive people away. Whichever of you leads the people in prayer should make it brief, for among them are the weak, the elderly and those with a need.”

notes: The oath, unnamed person, morning-prayer wording, exceptional anger in admonition and the weak/elderly/need clauses remain. Qays’s I heard and Abu Mas‘ud informed me remain exact; no full narrator names are supplied from outside the selected chain.

segments.arabic: [671] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا صلى أحدكم للناس فليخفف فإن منهم الضعيف والسقيم والكبير وإذا صلى أحدكم لنفسه فليطول ما شاء
segments.english: “When one of you leads the people in prayer, he should make it light, for among them are the weak, the sick and the elderly. When one of you prays by himself, he may prolong it as much as he wishes.”

notes: The distinct weak, sick and elderly categories and the separate permission for praying alone remain. The chain’s Malik informed us remains distinct from related to us.

segments.arabic: [672] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف حدثنا سفيان عن إسماعيل بن أبي خالد عن قيس بن أبي حازم عن أبي مسعود قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. Sufyan related to us, from Isma‘il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Mas‘ud, who said:

segments.arabic: قال رجل يا رسول الله إني لأتأخر عن الصلاة في الفجر مما يطيل بنا فلان فيها فغضب رسول الله ﷺ ما رأيته غضب في موضع كان أشد غضبا منه يومئذ، ثم قال: يا أيها الناس إن منكم منفرين فمن أم الناس فليتجوز فإن خلفه الضعيف والكبير وذا الحاجة
segments.english: A man said: “Messenger of Allah, I stay away from the dawn prayer because so-and-so makes it so long for us.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became angry. I had never seen him more angry in any situation than he was that day. Then he said: “People, some of you drive people away. Whoever leads the people should make it brief, for behind him are the weak, the elderly and those with a need.”

notes: This independently numbered repetition keeps the full chain and selected wording. It has no oath, unlike 670 and Bewley’s 672 comparison. In any situation follows the selected digital and modern reading; the historical print has in admonition. No oath or changed setting is inserted.

segments.arabic: [673] حدثنا آدم بن أبي إياس قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا محارب بن دثار قال: سمعت جابر بن عبد الله الأنصارى قال
segments.english: Adam ibn Abi Iyas related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Muharib ibn Dithar related to us. He said: I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Ansari say:

segments.arabic: أقبل رجل بناضحين وقد جنح الليل فوافق معاذا يصلي فترك ناضحه وأقبل إلى معاذ فقرأ بسورة البقرة أو النساء فانطلق الرجل وبلغه أن معاذا نال منه فأتى النبي ﷺ فشكا إليه معاذا، فقال النبي ﷺ يا معاذ أفتان أنت أو فاتن ثلاث مرار فلولا صليت ب { سبح اسم ربك } والشمس وضحاها والليل إذا يغشى فإنه يصلي وراءك الكبير والضعيف وذو الحاجة
segments.english: A man approached with two water-carrying camels when night had fallen. He found Mu‘adh praying, so he left his camel and went towards Mu‘adh. He recited Surat al-Baqarah or al-Nisa’. The man left, and word reached him that Mu‘adh had spoken against him. He went to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and complained to him about Mu‘adh. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Mu‘adh, are you one who repeatedly causes trial—or one who causes trial?”—three times. “Why did you not pray with ‘Glorify the name of your Lord,’ ‘By the sun and its brightness,’ and ‘By the night when it covers’? For behind you pray the elderly, the weak and those with a need.”

segments.arabic: أحسب في الحديث
segments.english: I think this is in the hadith.

segments.arabic: قال أبو عبد الله وتابعه سعيد بن مسروق ومسعر والشيباني قال عمرو وعبيد الله بن مقسم وأبو الزبير عن جابر قرأ معاذ في العشاء بالبقرة وتابعه الأعمش عن محارب
segments.english: Abu ‘Abd Allah said: Sa‘id ibn Masruq, Mis‘ar and al-Shaybani followed him in narrating it. ‘Amr, ‘Ubayd Allah ibn Miqsam and Abu al-Zubayr said, from Jabir: Mu‘adh recited al-Baqarah in ‘Isha’. Al-A‘mash followed him in narrating it from Muharib.

notes: The opening has two water-carrying camels, but the selected later noun is singular his camel; both are retained. The historical print has the later noun in the dual. The surah uncertainty, alternative fattan/fatin expression and three-times marker remain; the marker is not expanded into newly repeated quoted words.

Only the selected Quran fragments are translated; Most High from the historical print and verse/surah numbers from comparison aids are not inserted. The selected conjunction between all three fragments is and. The unnamed narrator’s I think this is in the hadith remains separate from prophetic speech, followed by the explicit Abu ‘Abd Allah attribution and all named supplementary transmitters and routes. Ibn Hajar identifies the uncertainty with Shu‘bah, but that external identification is not inserted into the source wording.

The selected closing report explicitly names al-Baqarah in Isha, while the opening retains al-Baqarah or al-Nisa. Bewley abbreviates the routes and its final Muharib attribution does not preserve al-A‘mash from Muharib; Khan omits most closing evidence. The complete selected source remains.

segments.arabic: [674] حدثنا أبو معمر قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز عن أنس قال:
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يوجز الصلاة ويكملها
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to make the prayer brief and complete it.

segments.arabic: [675] حدثنا إبراهيم بن موسى قال: أخبرنا الوليد قال: حدثنا الأوزاعي عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه أبي قتادة عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn Musa related to us. He said: Al-Walid informed us. He said: Al-Awza‘i related to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father Abu Qatadah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إني لأقوم في الصلاة أريد أن أطول فيها فأسمع بكاء الصبي فأتجوز في صلاتي كراهية أن أشق على أمه
segments.english: “I stand in prayer intending to prolong it, then hear a child crying and make my prayer brief, disliking to cause hardship to his mother.”

segments.arabic: تابعه بشر بن بكر وابن المبارك وبقية عن الأوزاعي
segments.english: Bishr ibn Bakr, Ibn al-Mubarak and Baqiyyah followed him in narrating it from al-Awza‘i.

notes: The full Abu Qatadah chain and the complete closing Bishr ibn Bakr/Ibn al-Mubarak/Baqiyyah route from al-Awza‘i remain. Khan omits the closing route; Bewley retains its names. The dislike of hardship to the mother remains.

segments.arabic: [676] حدثنا خالد بن مخلد قال: حدثنا سليمان بن بلال قال: حدثنا شريك بن عبد الله قال: سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول:
segments.english: Khalid ibn Makhlad related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Bilal related to us. He said: Sharik ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say:

segments.arabic: ما صليت وراء إمام قط أخف صلاة ولا أتم من النبي ﷺ وإن كان ليسمع بكاء الصبي فيخفف مخافة أن تفتن أمه
segments.english: I never prayed behind an imam whose prayer was lighter or more complete than that of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He would hear a child crying and make it light, fearing that his mother would be distressed.

notes: The full chain, never, lighter-or-more-complete comparison and fear for the mother remain. Distressed is the working rendering of تفتن; this does not add a new explanation to the saying.

segments.arabic: [677] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا يزيد بن زريع قال: حدثنا سعيد قال: حدثنا قتادة أن أنس بن مالك حدثه أن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ related to us. He said: Sa‘id related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us that Anas ibn Malik related to him that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إني لأدخل في الصلاة وأنا أريد إطالتها فأسمع بكاء الصبي فأتجوز في صلاتي مما أعلم من شدة وجد أمه من بكائه
segments.english: “I begin the prayer intending to prolong it, then hear a child crying and make my prayer brief, knowing the intensity of his mother’s distress at his crying.”

notes: Anas related to him remains explicit in the chain, as do the intention to prolong, the child’s cry and the intensity of the mother’s distress. The historical print calls him the Prophet of Allah, while the selected digital and modern print say the Prophet; no additional title is inserted.

segments.arabic: [678] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا ابن أبي عدي عن سعيد عن قتادة عن أنس بن مالك عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ibn Abi ‘Adi related to us, from Sa‘id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إني لأدخل في الصلاة فأريد إطالتها فأسمع بكاء الصبي فأتجوز مما أعلم من شدة وجد أمه من بكائه،
segments.english: “I begin the prayer and wish to prolong it, then hear a child crying and make it brief, knowing the intensity of his mother’s distress at his crying.”

segments.arabic: وقال موسى حدثنا أبان حدثنا قتادة حدثنا أنس عن النبي ﷺ مثله
segments.english: And Musa said: Aban related to us. Qatadah related to us. Anas related to us, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the like of it.

segments.arabic: [679] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب وأبو النعمان قالا: حدثنا حماد بن زيد عن أيوب عن عمرو بن دينار عن جابر قال:
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb and Abu al-Nu‘man related to us. They said: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir, who said:

segments.arabic: كان معاذ يصلي مع النبي ﷺ ثم يأتي قومه فيصلي بهم
segments.english: Mu‘adh used to pray with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then go to his people and lead them in prayer.

notes: Both opening teachers, Sulayman ibn Harb and Abu al-Nu‘man, and they said remain. The selected chain names Jabir without adding ibn Abd Allah from the Khan label. The report does not name the prayer or add an intention for either performance.

segments.arabic: [680] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن داود قال: حدثنا الأعمش عن إبراهيم عن الأسود عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها قالت
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: ‘Abd Allah ibn Dawud related to us. He said: Al-A‘mash related to us, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, who said:

segments.arabic: لما مرض النبي ﷺ مرضه الذي مات فيه أتاه يؤذنه بالصلاة، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل قلت: إن أبا بكر رجل أسيف إن يقم مقامك يبك فلا يقدر على القراءة قال مروا أبا بكر فليصل فقلت: مثله، فقال في الثالثة أو الرابعة إنكن صواحب يوسف مروا أبا بكر فليصل فصلى وخرج النبي ﷺ يهادى بين رجلين كأني أنظر إليه يخط برجليه الأرض فلما رآه أبو بكر ذهب يتأخر فأشار إليه أن صل فتأخر أبو بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه وقعد النبي ﷺ إلى جنبه وأبو بكر يسمع الناس التكبير
segments.english: When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became ill with the illness in which he died, someone came to inform him of the prayer. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.” I said: “Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. If he stands in your place, he will weep and be unable to recite.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.” I said the same. On the third or fourth occasion, he said: “You are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the prayer.” He led the prayer, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out supported between two men. It is as if I can see him tracing the ground with his feet. When Abu Bakr saw him, he began to move back. He gestured to him to pray. Abu Bakr, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, moved back, and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sat beside him, while Abu Bakr made the people hear the takbir.

segments.arabic: تابعه محاضر عن الأعمش
segments.english: Muhadir followed him in narrating it from al-A‘mash.

notes: The selected digital body does not name the person who came, whereas both inspected Arabic prints name Bilal. The working text keeps someone, as both English comparisons also do; a visible source notice records the printed name rather than silently adding it to the chosen wording.

Both selected personal honorifics and all three prophetic honorifics remain. The third-or-fourth uncertainty, I said the same, supported exit, movement back and audible takbir remain. There is no left-side specification in the selected body. The final route is Muhadir from al-A‘mash; Bewley drops Muhadir and Khan omits the note.

segments.arabic: [681] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا أبو معاوية عن الأعمش عن إبراهيم عن الأسود عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Abu Mu‘awiyah related to us, from al-A‘mash, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: لما ثقل رسول الله ﷺ جاء بلال يؤذنه بالصلاة، فقال مروا أبا بكر أن يصلي بالناس فقلت: يا رسول الله إن أبا بكر رجل أسيف وإنه متى ما يقم مقامك لا يسمع الناس فلو أمرت عمر، فقال مروا أبا بكر يصلي بالناس فقلت لحفصة قولي له إن أبا بكر رجل أسيف وإنه متى يقم مقامك لا يسمع الناس فلو أمرت عمر قال إنكن لأنتن صواحب يوسف مروا أبا بكر أن يصلي بالناس
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, became seriously ill, Bilal came to inform him of the prayer. He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” I said: “Messenger of Allah, Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. Whenever he stands in your place, he will not make the people hear. If only you would instruct ‘Umar.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” I said to Hafsah: “Tell him: ‘Abu Bakr is a tender-hearted man. Whenever he stands in your place, he will not make the people hear. If only you would instruct ‘Umar.’” He said: “Indeed, you are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.”

segments.arabic: فلما دخل في الصلاة وجد رسول الله ﷺ في نفسه خفة فقام يهادى بين رجلين ورجلاه تخطان في الأرض حتى دخل المسجد فلما سمع أبو بكر حسه ذهب أبو بكر يتأخر فأومأ إليه رسول الله ﷺ فجاء رسول الله ﷺ حتى جلس عن يسار أبي بكر فكان أبو بكر يصلي قائما وكان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي قاعدا يقتدي أبو بكر بصلاة رسول الله ﷺ والناس مقتدون بصلاة أبي بكر رضى الله تعالى عنه
segments.english: When he began the prayer, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt some relief. He rose, supported between two men, his feet tracing the ground, until he entered the mosque. When Abu Bakr heard his approach, Abu Bakr began to move back. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gestured to him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came until he sat on Abu Bakr’s left. Abu Bakr was praying standing, while the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was praying seated. Abu Bakr followed the prayer of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the people followed Abu Bakr’s prayer, may Allah Most High be pleased with him.

notes: All three commands and both objections remain. The selected text does not explicitly say Hafsah did so here, unlike an English comparison; it does explicitly say it in 684. The gesture here has no verbal instruction attached. Both are preserved without importing wording from the nearby accounts.

Both Arabic prints read ذهب أبو بكر يتأخر where the digital text has ذهب أبا بكر يتأخر. Only that case-form spelling is corrected with declared evidence and a visible original-preserving notice. The repeated Abu Bakr remains in English. All six prophetic honorifics and the final Abu Bakr honorific remain; the historical print additionally has an opening Aishah honorific not in the selected digital or modern wording.

segments.arabic: [682] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك بن أنس عن أيوب بن أبي تميمة السختياني عن محمد بن سيرين عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik ibn Anas, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah al-Sakhtiyani, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ انصرف من اثنتين، فقال له ذو اليدين أقصرت الصلاة أم نسيت يا رسول الله، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: أصدق ذو اليدين، فقال الناس نعم فقام رسول الله ﷺ فصلى اثنتين أخريين ثم سلم ثم كبر فسجد مثل سجوده أو أطول
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, finished after two. Dhu al-Yadayn said to him: “Has the prayer been shortened, or have you forgotten, Messenger of Allah?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Has Dhu al-Yadayn spoken the truth?” The people said: “Yes.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and prayed two more, then gave the salutation of peace. Then he said the takbir and prostrated as he had prostrated, or longer.

notes: The opening two and two more remain as selected, without adding the original expected total or a named prayer. The final selected verb states prostration without the number two; the Khan comparison supplies two prostrations, which belongs explicitly to the next selected report 683 and is not imported here. The direct question to the Messenger and the longer alternative remain. The historical chain has Abu Ayyub, while the digital and modern chain have Ayyub.

segments.arabic: [683] حدثنا أبو الوليد قال: حدثنا شعبة عن سعد بن إبراهيم عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة قال
segments.english: Abu al-Walid related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Sa‘d ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى النبي ﷺ الظهر ركعتين فقيل صليت ركعتين فصلى ركعتين ثم سلم ثم سجد سجدتين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed two rak‘ahs of Zuhr. He was told: “You prayed two rak‘ahs.” He prayed two rak‘ahs, then gave the salutation of peace, then performed two prostrations.

notes: Zuhr, both stated pairs of rak‘ahs, the quoted correction, salutation and two prostrations remain. No expected original total is inserted.

segments.arabic: [684] حدثنا إسماعيل قال: حدثنا مالك بن أنس عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أم المؤمنين
segments.english: Isma‘il related to us. He said: Malik ibn Anas related to us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, Mother of the Believers:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ قال في مرضه مروا أبا بكر يصلي بالناس قالت عائشة قلت: إن أبا بكر إذا قام في مقامك لم يسمع الناس من البكاء فمر عمر فليصل، فقال مروا أبا بكر فليصل للناس قالت عائشة لحفصة قولي له إن أبا بكر إذا قام في مقامك لم يسمع الناس من البكاء فمر عمر فليصل للناس ففعلت حفصة، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: مه إنكن لأنتن صواحب يوسف مروا أبا بكر فليصل للناس قالت حفصة لعائشة ما كنت لأصيب منك خيرا
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said during his illness: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said: I said: “If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the prayer.” He said: “Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” ‘A’ishah said to Hafsah: “Say to him: ‘If Abu Bakr stands in your place, he will not make the people hear because of his weeping, so tell ‘Umar to lead the people in prayer.’” Hafsah did so. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Stop! Indeed, you are the women associated with Yusuf. Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer.” Hafsah said to ‘A’ishah: “I was never to get any good from you.”

segments.arabic: [685] حدثنا أبو الوليد هشام بن عبد الملك قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني عمرو بن مرة قال: سمعت سالم بن أبي الجعد قال: سمعت النعمان بن بشير يقول: قال النبي ﷺ

segments.arabic: [687] حدثنا أحمد بن أبي رجاء قال: حدثنا معاوية بن عمرو قال: حدثنا زائدة بن قدامة قال: حدثنا حميد الطويل حدثنا أنس قال
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Abi Raja’ related to us. He said: Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Amr related to us. He said: Za’idah ibn Qudamah related to us. He said: Humayd al-Tawil related to us. Anas related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: أقيمت الصلاة فأقبل علينا رسول الله ﷺ بوجهه، فقال أقيموا صفوفكم وتراصوا فإني أراكم من وراء ظهري

segments.arabic: [688] حدثنا أبو عاصم عن مالك عن سمي عن أبي صالح عن أبي هريرة قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Abu ‘Asim related to us, from Malik, from Sumayy, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: الشهداء الغرق والمطعون والمبطون والهدم، وقال ولو يعلمون ما في التهجير لاستبقوا ولو يعلمون ما في العتمة والصبح لأتوهما ولو حبوا ولو يعلمون ما في الصف المقدم لاستهموا
segments.english: “The martyrs are: one who drowns, one who dies of plague, one who dies of an abdominal illness, and one who dies under a collapsed structure.” And he said: “If they knew what there is in going early, they would race to it. If they knew what there is in ‘Isha’ and the dawn prayer, they would come to them even crawling. If they knew what there is in the foremost row, they would draw lots.”

notes: The four selected martyr categories remain in digital/modern order; the historical print places abdominal illness before plague. No fifth category is imported from 624. The modern print numbers the second statement separately as 721 after 720; the selected digital report remains one complete entry.

Going early retains the selected phrase without inserting Zuhr or its early time. The selected final condition names only the foremost row; the adhan phrase added in Bewley’s comparison is not inserted. All three conditions, racing, crawling and drawing lots remain.

segments.arabic: [689] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا عبد الرزاق قال: أخبرنا معمر عن همام عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us. He said: Ma‘mar informed us, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

segments.arabic: إنما جعل الإمام ليؤتم به فلا تختلفوا عليه فإذا ركع فاركعوا وإذا قال سمع الله لمن حمده فقولوا ربنا لك الحمد وإذا سجد فاسجدوا وإذا صلى جالسا فصلوا جلوسا أجمعون وأقيموا الصف في الصلاة فإن إقامة الصف من حسن الصلاة
segments.english: “The imam is appointed only to be followed, so do not differ from him. When he bows, bow. When he says, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him,’ say, ‘Our Lord, to You belongs praise.’ When he prostrates, prostrate. When he prays sitting, all of you pray sitting. Straighten the row in prayer, for straightening the row is part of the excellence of prayer.”

notes: The full chain and all follow-the-imam clauses remain. The praise formula here lacks the and in 657; it remains Our Lord, to You belongs praise. Straightening the singular row and the source’s excellence wording remain rather than importing the comparison’s expanded correct-and-perfect wording.

segments.arabic: [691] حدثنا معاذ بن أسد قال: أخبرني الفضل بن موسى قال: أخبرنا سعيد بن عبيد الطائي عن بشير بن يسار الأنصارى عن أنس بن مالك
segments.english: Mu‘adh ibn Asad related to us. He said: Al-Fadl ibn Musa informed me. He said: Sa‘id ibn ‘Ubayd al-Ta’i informed us, from Bashir ibn Yasar al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أنه قدم المدينة فقيل له ما أنكرت منا منذ يوم عهدت رسول الله ﷺ قال: ما أنكرت شيئا إلا أنكم لا تقيمون الصفوف،
segments.english: That he came to Madinah and was asked: “What have you disapproved of among us since the time you knew the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace?” He said: “I have disapproved of nothing except that you do not straighten the rows.”

segments.arabic: وقال عقبة بن عبيد عن بشير بن يسار قدم علينا أنس بن مالك المدينة بهذا
segments.english: And ‘Uqbah ibn ‘Ubayd said, from Bashir ibn Yasar: Anas ibn Malik came to us in Madinah—with this account.

notes: The selected chain says al-Fadl informed me; the historical print says related to us and the modern print informed us. These differences are recorded without rewriting the selected transmission verb. The first account remains third-person, unlike Khan’s first-person rendering. segments.arabic: [693] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا داود عن عمرو بن دينار عن كريب مولى ابن عباس عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Dawud related to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Kurayb, the freedman of Ibn ‘Abbas, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: صليت مع النبي ﷺ ذات ليلة فقمت عن يساره فأخذ رسول الله ﷺ برأسي من ورائي فجعلني عن يمينه فصلى ورقد فجاءه المؤذن فقام وصلى ولم يتوضأ
segments.english: I prayed with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, one night and stood on his left. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took hold of my head from behind me and placed me on his right. He prayed and slept. The caller came to him, and he rose and prayed without performing ablution.

segments.arabic: [695] حدثنا موسى حدثنا ثابت بن يزيد حدثنا عاصم عن الشعبي عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال
segments.english: Musa related to us. Thabit ibn Yazid related to us. ‘Asim related to us, from al-Sha‘bi, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, who said:

segments.arabic: قمت ليلة أصلي عن يسار النبي ﷺ فأخذ بيدي أو بعضدي حتى أقامني عن يمينه، وقال بيده من ورائي
segments.english: One night I stood to pray on the left of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He took me by my hand—or my upper arm—until he placed me on his right, and he reached with his hand from behind me.

segments.arabic: [696] حدثنا محمد قال: أخبرنا عبدة عن يحيى بن سعيد الأنصارى عن عمرة عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abdah informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id al-Ansari, from ‘Amrah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي من الليل في حجرته وجدار الحجرة قصير فرأى الناس شخص النبي ﷺ فقام أناس يصلون بصلاته فأصبحوا فتحدثوا بذلك فقام ليلة الثانية فقام معه أناس يصلون بصلاته صنعوا ذلك ليلتين أو ثلاثا حتى إذا كان بعد ذلك جلس رسول الله ﷺ فلم يخرج فلما أصبح ذكر ذلك الناس، فقال إني خشيت أن تكتب عليكم صلاة الليل
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray at night in his room. The room’s wall was low, and the people saw the figure of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Some people stood and followed his prayer. In the morning they spoke about that. He stood the second night, and some people stood with him, following his prayer. They did that for two or three nights. After that, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained seated and did not come out. In the morning the people mentioned that. He said: “I feared that the night prayer would be prescribed for you.”

notes: The selected chain names Muhammad and ‘Abdah without expanding Muhammad’s name from the historical print. ‘Amrah, the low wall, visible figure, second night, two-or-three uncertainty, sitting/not coming out and prescribed night prayer remain. The comparison’s compulsory sense is retained without adding a morning question absent from the selected text.

segments.arabic: [697] حدثنا إبراهيم بن المنذر قال: حدثنا ابن أبي فديك قال: حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب عن المقبري عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن عائشة رضى الله تعالى عنها
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Fudayk related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from ‘A’ishah, may Allah Most High be pleased with her:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ كان له حصير يبسطه بالنهار ويحتجره بالليل فثاب إليه ناس فصلوا وراءه
segments.english: That the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had a mat which he spread out by day and used to enclose a space by night. People gathered to him and prayed behind him.

notes: The full Ibn Abi Fudayk/Ibn Abi Dhi’b/al-Maqburi/Abu Salamah route and Aishah’s complete honorific remain. The day/night uses of the mat remain; enclose a space renders يحتجره without changing the mat into a building. No at night expansion is added to the gathering clause.

segments.arabic: [698] حدثنا عبد الأعلى بن حماد قال: حدثنا وهيب قال: حدثنا موسى بن عقبة عن سالم أبي النضر عن بسر بن سعيد عن زيد بن ثابت
segments.english: ‘Abd al-A‘la ibn Hammad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us. He said: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah related to us, from Salim Abu al-Nadr, from Busr ibn Sa‘id, from Zayd ibn Thabit:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ اتخذ حجرة
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, made a small room—

segments.arabic: قال حسبت أنه قال من حصير
segments.english: He said: “I think he said: of a mat”—

segments.arabic: في رمضان فصلى فيها ليالي فصلى بصلاته ناس من أصحابه فلما علم بهم جعل يقعد فخرج إليهم، فقال قد عرفت الذي رأيت من صنيعكم فصلوا أيها الناس في بيوتكم فإن أفضل الصلاة صلاة المرء في بيته إلا المكتوبة
segments.english: in Ramadan. He prayed in it for several nights, and some of his Companions followed his prayer. When he became aware of them, he began to remain seated. He went out to them and said: “I have understood what I saw you doing. People, pray in your houses, for the best prayer is a person’s prayer in his house, except the prescribed prayer.”

segments.arabic: قال عفان حدثنا وهيب حدثنا موسى سمعت أبا النضر عن بسر عن زيد عن النبي ﷺ
segments.english: ‘Affan said: Wuhayb related to us. Musa related to us: I heard Abu al-Nadr, from Busr, from Zayd, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

notes: The mat uncertainty is separated from the report body and remains He said: I think he said. Neither the selected digital text nor the inspected prints names that speaker at this point; the English comparisons’ Sa‘id identification is not inserted. The Ramadan timing, several nights, some Companions, remaining seated, observed action and exception for prescribed prayer remain.

The complete ‘Affan/Wuhayb/Musa/I heard Abu al-Nadr/Busr/Zayd closing route with its own honorific remains visible and in the full script. Bewley reduces it to a different isnad and Khan omits it. No body is invented for the closing chain.
